children.module_doc:
Data centre facility — Zhang et al. 2025, Virginia hyperscale.
=============================================================================

Source and scope
----------------
Materials-production + operation inventory for a representative hyperscale
data centre (10,000 m² white space, Virginia US, SERC grid, PUE 1.4 baseline,
25-year operating life), from Zhang, M., Carbajales-Dale, M., Ma, X., Guo, L.,
Fan, C. (2025). "Cleaner grid or smarter cooling? Environmental impact
trade-offs of a data center using the life cycle assessment method." *Cleaner
Energy Systems* 12, 100223. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cles.2025.100223 —
quantities are from the paper's Table 1 / supplementary Table S1
(``...-mmc1.xlsx``); the search queries below are seeded from the exact
ecoinvent process names the paper cites in its own OpenLCA contribution
breakdown (``...-mmc2.xlsx``), then re-verified against this project's
ecoinvent 3.9.1 apos database.

Functional unit: **the whole facility over its 25-year operating life**
(1 unit), not a per-kWh or per-m² unit. ``baseline_grid.py`` splits it into a
fixed burden plus 1.60e9 kWh of electricity, and ``dc_inputs`` reads an IT
load out of that draw at the paper's PUE (``dc_config.DC_REFERENCE_PUE``).

**Boundary: Material Production + Construction + Operation.** Transportation
(delivery to site), Disposal and Recycling (including the avoided-burden
credits) are outside the study's boundary (ASSUMPTIONS.md §6). The
Construction-phase energy and water were also left out until 21 Oct 2026 as a
"scope choice"; they are in the source and inside the boundary, so they are
in. The full cradle-to-grave version (all 33 flows) is in git history and was
diffed against this module on 21 Oct (docs/SOURCE_DIFF.md).

**Validated** (full cradle-to-grave version, before the boundary was narrowed):
every pick was checked against a live search of ecoinvent 3.9.1 apos, and the
LCA on the resulting activity with IPCC 2021 GWP100 gave 8.38×10⁸ kg CO2-eq
against the paper's 9.63×10⁸ (ratio 0.87 — a good match given the different
ecoinvent version/system model and LCIA method to the paper's ecoinvent 3.7
cutoff + TRACI 2.1). Electricity dominates, so the narrower boundary should
land in the same ballpark; ``validate.data_centre_vs_paper()`` reports the
current ratio.

**Four deliberate substitutions**, because ecoinvent 3.9.1 has no exact
equivalent of what the paper's ecoinvent 3.7 cutoff model used, or because the
study's grid replaces the paper's:

- ``copper`` → the copper cathode market; Zhang's own dataset (mmc2) is
  ``market for metal part of electronics scrap, in copper, anode``, a scrap
  stream, which does not describe cabling. Order 1e5 kg CO2e over 25 years.
- construction electricity → the GB medium-voltage market, where the paper's
  operating electricity is on US-SERC; ``baseline_grid.py`` strips both out and
  puts the facility on the study's half-hourly GB series.

- ``battery`` → a specific chemistry (NMC111) standing in for the old
  undifferentiated "Li-ion, rechargeable, prismatic" market, which 3.9.1 has
  split by chemistry. Swap for LFP if the facility's real UPS chemistry is
  known — LFP is more typical for modern stationary storage.
- ``refrigerant_r134a`` → the paper's "Tetrafluoroethane" flow is R134a
  (1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane); 3.9.1 only has it under the refrigerant name.
- ``servers`` → ecoinvent's only embodied-manufacturing dataset for a generic
  server is ``market for computer, laptop`` — the same proxy the paper used
  (its own quantity is a server count with a refresh-cycle adjustment).

One direct biosphere flow, added 14 Oct 2026: the refrigerant leaked. Zhang's
supplementary Table S1 derives the 450 kg of R134a as "2 000 kg × 0.009 y⁻¹ ×
25 y = 450 kg top-up" — refrigerant bought to replace what leaked at 0.9 %/yr
— and the paper charges only its production (~6.6 kg CO2e/kg). A top-up that
replaces leakage is the leakage, so the same 450 kg is emitted as HFC-134a to
air (GWP100 1,530 in IPCC 2021): 688 t CO2e over the life, ~27.5 t/yr. Their
0.9 %/yr sits below the 1-3 %/yr they cite for best-practice sites, so this
errs low. The 2,000 kg initial charge is not in the inventory and its
end-of-life fate is outside the boundary.

children.source:
Grid-scale battery storage — Jasper et al. 2026 container, Voß et al. 2025 cell.
=============================================================================

Why this inventory exists
-------------------------
The battery used to be ecoinvent's ``market for battery, Li-ion, LFP,
rechargeable, prismatic`` [GLO]: an **electric-vehicle traction pack**
(Dai et al. / GREET lineage, 2016-era, 116 Wh/kg) with no container, racking,
HVAC or fire suppression — ``battery.CONTAINER_UPLIFT_FRACTION`` was 0.0 and
said so. A grid battery is neither of those things. It is large-format
prismatic cells in racks, in a 20 ft container, with its own thermal
management and fire suppression, and those non-cell parts are 18-23 % of the
DC block's carbon in every source that itemises them.
children.module_doc:
Grid-scale battery storage — Jasper et al. 2026 container, Voß et al. 2025 cell.
=============================================================================

Why this inventory exists
-------------------------
The battery used to be ecoinvent's ``market for battery, Li-ion, LFP,
rechargeable, prismatic`` [GLO]: an **electric-vehicle traction pack**
(Dai et al. / GREET lineage, 2016-era, 116 Wh/kg) with no container, racking,
HVAC or fire suppression — ``battery.CONTAINER_UPLIFT_FRACTION`` was 0.0 and
said so. A grid battery is neither of those things. It is large-format
prismatic cells in racks, in a 20 ft container, with its own thermal
management and fire suppression, and those non-cell parts are 18-23 % of the
DC block's carbon in every source that itemises them.

So the battery is assembled from two published inventories, the way the solar
plant and the step-up transformers are:

    container  F.B. Jasper, Y. Zhou, H. Ersoy, M. Baumann et al., "Life Cycle
               Assessment of Grid-Scale Battery Storage", Energy Advances 5
               (2026) 550-570, doi:10.1039/D5YA00341E. SI workbook (Zenodo
               doi:10.5281/zenodo.17651912), sheets "Air-cooled CSS -
               Production" and "Liquid-cooled CSS - Production". CC-BY-NC.
    cell       P. Voß, B. Gruber, M. Mitterfellner, J.-D. Plöpst, F. Degen,
               R. Schmuch, S. Lux, "Benchmarking state-of-the-art sodium-ion
               battery cells", Energy Environ. Sci. 18 (2025) 8104-8129,
               doi:10.1039/D5EE00415B. Main text Table 3 (the cell bill), ESI
               Tables S5, S31, S32, S35, S36 (the materials).

Jasper's own cell *is* Voß's: their workbook links ``LFP based LIB (Voß et
al.)`` at 176.6 Wh/kg and does not reproduce it. Voß is built on **ecoinvent
3.9.1** — this study's own database — so the cell rebuilds here without a
version mismatch, where Jasper re-scored it on 3.11.

Which of Jasper's designs
-------------------------
**Liquid-cooled LFP**: 1,600 kW / 3,008 kWh, eight racks of eight 47 kWh
modules, 306 Ah cells. Liquid cooling is what current containers ship with
(the Sungrow and Trina EPDs that sit beside this inventory are both
liquid-cooled); the air-cooled 2,064 kWh design is the older generation, and
the three sodium-ion chemistries are Jasper's comparison, not the market.
Current 20 ft products pack ~5 MWh; per-container items (container, fire
suppression, controller, part of the cooling) are ~7 kg CO2e/kWh here and would
be ~3 kg/kWh lower spread over 5 MWh. Built as published; the denser packing
is a sensitivity, not an invented design.

Choices this study makes, not the sources
-----------------------------------------
* **Cells made in China** (``CELL_FACTORY``). Voß model a German gigafactory;
  Jasper assume Chinese production, and Chinese makers supply most stationary
  LFP cells. The German cell is built too, as ``bess_lfp_cell_1kwh_de``, so
  Voß's own published figure can be reproduced (``describe()``).
* **Graphite 75:25 synthetic:natural** (``GRAPHITE_SYNTHETIC_SHARE``), Voß's
  benchmark, which they give as current market share. Jasper's 65:35 is
  ecoinvent 3.11's default mix, not a market statement.
* **Cell factory energy 18 kWh electricity + 19 kWh natural gas per kWh of
  cells**, Degen et al. (2023) as restated by Jasper §2.4.1. Voß do not
  tabulate it. The gas is charged as heat delivered (19 kWh = 68.4 MJ).

What is deliberately NOT here — the study's own boundary
--------------------------------------------------------
* **End-of-life**, as everywhere (ASSUMPTIONS.md §6). Jasper's
  ``treatment of used CSS`` and the whole EOL sheet are not taken.
* **Transport to site.** The study excludes delivery to site and nothing else,
  because the site is not known; upstream transport is in. Jasper's rows split
  on exactly that line (see ``_no_transport`` below): his 1,000 km lorry +
  8,000 km sea + 1,000 km rail legs ship finished parts from China to his
  German site and are left out, as ``upv.py`` leaves out Smith's A14; his
  100 km lorry + 600 km rail legs bring materials to the module and rack
  factories and are kept. Voß's China-to-Berlin legs (18.5 t·km sea, 1.0 and
  0.7 t·km lorry per kg) carry materials to *their* German factory, which this
  China-made cell does not have, so they are not taken. The Chinese lorry leg
  is carried on every cell material (ESI §3.1.3 add it "additionally" to
  each), the natural graphite included: Voß's 5.19 kg CO₂e/kg is their figure
  before transport (the main text's 5.7 is 5.19 plus the three legs).
* **The power conversion system** (800 kg), charged separately by
  ``battery.PCS_ACTIVITY`` on the power term.
* **The battery transformer** (5,500 kg). Charged separately since 15 Oct, per
  MW of ``cap_batt_p``, by ``optimisation/transformers.py``: its mass from this
  bill, its composition from the IEA PVPS unit
  (``stepup_transformers.CSS_TX_KG``, which ``check()`` holds to this row).
  Jasper's own per-kg recipe (Hunziker 2020, a 630 kVA unit with an on-load
  tap changer) is set aside as a stated substitution; see stepup_transformers.
* **Voß's processing materials** (NMP, argon, nitrogen, compressed air), which
  they draw from Degen's source data and do not tabulate. Small; this errs low.

Factors that are pinned, not inventories
----------------------------------------
Five figures in the sources are carbon footprints rather than exchanges. Each
enters as a ``Carbon dioxide, fossil`` emission of its own size, so it is
correct for GWP100 and *only* for GWP100 — do not read other impact
categories off those five activities:

    natural graphite   5.19 kg CO2e/kg   Engels et al. 2022 via Voß §3.1.1.2,
                                         less the transport legs Voß added
    PVDF binder       60.6  kg CO2e/kg   Hu et al. via Voß §3.1.3.1
    separator          5.06 kg CO2e/kg   ecoinvent 3.8, as Voß §3.1.3.4 chose
                                         over 3.9.1's 39.6 ("unrealistically
                                         high"); 3.9.1 here scores 34.4-39.5
    graphitisation crucible  7.346 kg CO2e per kg SGr   Carrère via Voß Table S5
    packaging media + block  0.432 kg CO2e per kg SGr   Carrère via Voß Table S5

Units
-----
The functional unit, ``bess_dc_block_per_kwh``, is per kWh of **nameplate** (cell) capacity, which is
what both sources report. ``optimisation/battery.py`` divides by its
``USABLE_FRACTION`` because the LP's ``cap_batt_e`` is the energy the battery
can actually swing.

children.source:
PEM fuel cell — Babatunde 2024 stack, Usai 2021 balance of plant, 1 kWh from it.
=============================================================================

Four activities in one database:
children.module_doc:
PEM fuel cell — Babatunde 2024 stack, Usai 2021 balance of plant, 1 kWh from it.
=============================================================================

Four activities in one database:

* ``pemfc_stack_1kw_babatunde`` — cradle-to-gate manufacture of **one 1 kW
  PEM fuel cell stack**, transcribed from the paper's supplementary Table S1.
* ``pemfc_bop_stationary_1kw`` — the **balance of plant for 1 kW** of a
  stationary, hydrogen-fed unit: Usai et al. 2021's process loops, plus an
  inverter and a share of a container.
* ``pemfc_service_stationary_1kw`` — **one service of 1 kW**: air filter and
  coolant.
* ``pemfc_op_1kwh_h2`` — **1 kWh of net AC electricity, low voltage**, from a
  1 kW hydrogen-fed PEMFC system: hydrogen, and the three above amortised.

Stack — source and scope
------------------------
Babatunde, O.M., Akintayo, B.D., Emezirinwune, M.U., Olanrewaju, O.A. (2024).
"Environmental Impact Assessment of a 1 kW Proton-Exchange Membrane Fuel
Cell: A Mid-Point and End-Point Analysis." *Hydrogen* 5(2), 352–373.
https://doi.org/10.3390/hydrogen5020020 — supplementary Table S1 documents
the ecoinvent 3.7.1 dataset ``fuel cell production, stack polymer electrolyte
membrane, 2kW electrical, future`` that the study runs in SimaPro 9.2 with
ReCiPe 2016. Manufacturing only: the paper's 32,000 h operating life is
stated in its scope but nothing operational is inventoried.

**Two scale factors, both deliberate.** ``FC_SCALE`` is the product of:

1. ``FC_KW_SCALE = 0.5`` — Table S1's reference product is a 2 kW stack but
   the paper reports everything per 1 kW. Halving is what the paper itself
   did: every value in its Tables S2–S4 is about 2× the corresponding
   value in its headline Tables 3–5.
2. ``FC_S1_SCALE = 1.878606235`` — Table S1 as printed does **not** reproduce
   the paper's own results. Every amount is smaller than the live ecoinvent
   dataset it documents by this uniform factor (verified exchange by
   exchange: activated carbon 0.0008 vs 0.00150288, aluminium 0.3 vs
   0.563582, graphite 4.5 vs 8.45373, platinum 0.00075 vs 0.00140895,
   electricity 16.9 vs 31.748 kWh — identical to 9 significant figures).
   At face value the inventory reproduces only ~53 % of the paper's impacts;
   scaled, it reproduces them. A defect in the published table, not a
   modelling choice — amounts below stay as printed so they can be checked
   against the PDF, and the correction is applied once at write time.

**Validated against the paper** (``validate.fc_stack_vs_paper``): on ReCiPe
2016 v1.03 (H), damage totals 1.00 / 0.99 / 1.10 of the paper's Table 5,
mid-point median ratio 1.003 over 18 categories, end-point 1.013 over 22.
The misses (ecotoxicity, metal resources, land and water use) are the
categories whose factors changed most between ecoinvent 3.7.1 and 3.9.1.

**One substitution:** Table S1 prints one aggregated electricity row and one
heat row; the ecoinvent dataset splits them over regional markets. The GLO
market groups are used for both — the single-row equivalent of what the
paper prints — and reproduce the combustion-driven categories to ~1–2 %.

Table S1's two "by-products" are waste sent for treatment, so negative
technosphere amounts against the waste markets (ecoinvent's own convention).

Operation — source and scope
----------------------------
Functional unit 1 kWh net AC. Every parameter is a literature value, not a
fitted one:

1. **Hydrogen** = 1 / (η × LHV), with η a *net AC* efficiency so parasitic
   loads (air compressor, pumps, controls, inverter) are inside it.
   ``FC_ETA_NET_BOL = 0.50`` LHV is bracketed by DOE's stationary 1–25 kWe
   target of ≥45 % (on natural gas, so including reformer losses a pure-H2
   system does not pay), a reported ~51.6 % for a 1 kW H2-fed PEMFC, and the
   ~50 % usually quoted for mid-size stationary PEMFC; 0.45–0.55 is the
   defensible range and ±0.05 moves the result ±10 %. The 0.95 derate follows
   the convention that end of life is a 10 % drop in cell voltage (Stropnik
   et al. 2022); degrading linearly puts the lifetime mean at 95 % of BOL.
2. **Stack** = 1 / (1 kW × 30,000 h). Stationary H2 PEM stacks are refurbished
   at 24-30k running hours (Nedstack datasheets); Bionaz et al. 2022 use 40k;
   Babatunde's 32k is ecoinvent's own figure, not an independent one.
3. **Balance of plant** = ``pemfc_bop_stationary_1kw`` below, over 80,000 h
   (DOE's 100 kW-3 MW stationary class, and ecoinvent's own system life).
4. **Maintenance** = ``pemfc_service_stationary_1kw`` below, once per 8,000 h.

Balance of plant — source and scope
-----------------------------------
This used to be ecoinvent's ``fuel cell production, polymer electrolyte
membrane, 2kW electrical, future`` net of its stack: a **natural-gas domestic
micro-CHP** ("operation with connection to low pressure gas network"), carrying
fuel-processor items, a hot-water kit and 400 km of installer driving, scaled
linearly from 2 kW to MW. 469 t CO2e per MW. Its maintenance was reformer-
catalyst replacement. None of it describes a hydrogen-fed MW-class unit.

No published inventory does, either. A 2026 systematic review (Energies
19:3808) finds BoP inventories still "simplified using obsolete" bills; the
only H2-fed *stationary* system with a component bill is a 3 kW UPS (Stropnik
et al. 2018, Energy 165:824), and every heavy-duty LCA (Gentilucci et al.
2024, SAE 2024-24-0020, 200 kW; Syré et al. 2024, WEVJ 15:114) reuses an
automotive one. So the BoP is assembled, the way the battery is:

**Process loops — Usai et al. 2021**, J Cleaner Prod 280:125086, SI Table 1
(``usai 2021 fc lci per kw.pdf``): an 80 kW H2 PEM system, per kW net, every
line already named as an ecoinvent process. Air (compression-expansion motor,
filter, ducting, sensor), water (humidifier, Nafion tubes, pre-cooler,
demister), heat (fan, pumps, radiators, antifreeze), fuel (blower, ejectors,
pipes), controller, wiring, frame, fasteners. Two amounts are per *system* in
the printed table though labelled per kW — the 3 coolant pumps and 16 m of
wiring (Miotti's per-system figure) — and are divided by 80 here; as printed
they rebuild Usai's own heat and "other" results 17x and 35x over. Everything
else is as printed. Rebuilt on 3.9.1 the loops come to ~82 % of Usai's own
854 kg CO2e/80 kW (their results workbook): the table rounds to two decimals,
which loses most of the radiator and controller (0.27 and 0.63 of Usai).

**What a vehicle has and a container does not, and the reverse.** The
compression-expansion motor stands in for a stationary air blower (heavier,
so it errs high); the belly pan stands in for the module frame. Added for a
stationary unit, neither of which a vehicle FC system carries:
- *power conversion*: ecoinvent's 500 kW inverter, the dataset the battery's
  power term uses. The vehicle's DC/DC boost sits in its drivetrain, not its
  FC system, so nothing is counted twice.
- *enclosure*: the battery's own fire-lined 20 ft container (Jasper et al.
  2026, ``bess.py``), one per ``FC_KW_PER_CONTAINER`` = 1 MW. ASSUMED - no
  source states MW per container for fuel cells.

**Maintenance** is what an H2-fed unit actually consumes: an air filter and
a coolant change per service (Usai's own amounts), every 8,000 h (ASSUMED;
Battelle 2016 gives a one-year interval for backup units). No reformer
catalyst, no platinum top-up, no installer driving. Stack replacement is not
maintenance: it is the stack line, on the optimiser's max(calendar, duty)
rule.

**Benchmarks**, whole systems cradle-to-gate per kW: Usai 37.6 (no tank),
Miotti 29, Gentilucci 30.5-51.4 (200 kW HD), Ballard 73 (70 kW module, its own
note), Stropnik/Bionaz 405 (3 kW UPS). The vehicle figures carry no inverter
or enclosure; this one does, and its stack (Babatunde's 2 kW graphite-plate
unit) is heavier than any automotive stack.

**No direct biosphere flows — deliberately.** A hydrogen PEMFC emits only
water, and it is not inventoried, for the same reason ecoinvent's own PEMFC
operation datasets do not: the product water is the electrolyser's feed water
coming back out, already counted as consumed upstream. Adding it as a
``Water → air`` emission would double-count (ReCiPe's water-use factor for
water emitted to air is +1.0).

Boundary, as everywhere in this study: cradle-to-gate, no end-of-life, no
delivery transport.

What the optimiser reads: ``optimisation/fuel_cell.py`` splits the operation
activity into stack (per MW, replaced on max(calendar, duty)), balance of
plant (likewise) and maintenance (per MWh), and excludes the hydrogen, which
the LP supplies explicitly.

children.source:
Hydrogen storage tank — Gandiglio et al. 2022, a steel vessel.
=============================================================================

Source and scope
----------------
    M. Gandiglio, P. Marocco, I. Bianco, D. Lovera, G.A. Blengini, M. Santarelli,
    "Life cycle assessment of a renewable energy system with hydrogen-battery
    storage for a remote off-grid community", Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 47 (2022)
    32822-32834. Table 5 (p. 32828): the hydrogen tank is one line, 15,652 kg of
    "Steel, chromium steel 18/8 {GLO}" for a 21.6 m³ vessel at 28 bar, over the
    plant's 25-year life, charged once.
children.module_doc:
Hydrogen storage tank — Gandiglio et al. 2022, a steel vessel.
=============================================================================

Source and scope
----------------
    M. Gandiglio, P. Marocco, I. Bianco, D. Lovera, G.A. Blengini, M. Santarelli,
    "Life cycle assessment of a renewable energy system with hydrogen-battery
    storage for a remote off-grid community", Int. J. Hydrogen Energy 47 (2022)
    32822-32834. Table 5 (p. 32828): the hydrogen tank is one line, 15,652 kg of
    "Steel, chromium steel 18/8 {GLO}" for a 21.6 m³ vessel at 28 bar, over the
    plant's 25-year life, charged once.

ecoinvent 3.9.1 has no hydrogen storage vessel of any kind, so the tank is
built from that line. **Functional unit: 1 kg of hydrogen storage capacity.**
The paper's 21.6 m³ at 28 bar and 15 °C holds 50.0 kg of hydrogen
(``capacity_kg()``, real gas), so its vessel is 313 kg of stainless steel per
kg stored; ``optimisation/h2_storage.py`` amortises that over
``dc_config.TANK_LIFETIME_YEARS``.

**Boundary.** In: the shell (Gandiglio), its forming (ADDED, 22 Oct 2026: a
pressure vessel is rolled and welded, which the paper's steel line does not
cover; sheet rolling of chromium steel on the shell mass, average metal working
being the sensitivity case — CUTOFF_RULE_PLAN.md step 5), and the frame and
foundation pad (ASSUMED from the vessel's geometry, 14 Oct 2026: a 0.5 m slab
with 0.5 m clearance, rebar at 100 kg/m³, saddles and frame at 10 % of the
shell). Out: end-of-life, delivery to site, and the hydrogen itself (leakage is
the LP's ``H2 leaked from tank`` term). Valves, pipework and compressor hardware
are unsourced and sit on the cut-off register (``optimiser_lca/exclusions.py``).

**Two designs.** ``gandiglio_28bar`` is the paper's low-pressure buffer, heavy
per kg because at 28 bar the steel is set by volume, not hoop stress; a Type I
seamless cylinder at 200 bar reaches ~1 wt%, three times lighter, and needs
2.5 kWh/kg of compression (charged in the dispatch, not here). ``TANK_DESIGN``
picks which is built; the paper's is the default because it has a published
inventory behind it.

children.name: Hydrogen storage tank, steel vessel, per kg capacity (gandiglio_28bar)
transformer foreground — stepup_transformers.py
children.source:
Power transformers — Leng et al. 2026 (wind step-ups and the grid intake),
IEA PVPS 2026 (solar step-ups).
=============================================================================

Why this inventory exists
-------------------------
A wind turbine generates at **690 V**, which is *low* voltage (<1 kV, the band
ecoinvent itself draws). A PV inverter's terminals are 400 V. The data centre
draws at *medium* voltage, 1–24 kV, because that is the level ``market for
electricity, medium voltage`` describes and the level the Zhang foreground is
authored against. Something has to bridge those, and it is not optional:
100 MW at 690 V is 83,674 A, which is not a cable. So every turbine carries its
own transformer at the foot of its tower — one per turbine, not one per farm —
and every PV inverter station carries one.
children.module_doc:
Power transformers — Leng et al. 2026 (wind step-ups and the grid intake),
IEA PVPS 2026 (solar step-ups).
=============================================================================

Why this inventory exists
-------------------------
A wind turbine generates at **690 V**, which is *low* voltage (<1 kV, the band
ecoinvent itself draws). A PV inverter's terminals are 400 V. The data centre
draws at *medium* voltage, 1–24 kV, because that is the level ``market for
electricity, medium voltage`` describes and the level the Zhang foreground is
authored against. Something has to bridge those, and it is not optional:
100 MW at 690 V is 83,674 A, which is not a cable. So every turbine carries its
own transformer at the foot of its tower — one per turbine, not one per farm —
and every PV inverter station carries one.

**It is a gap, not a double count.** ecoinvent's ``wind turbine construction,
2MW, onshore`` lists its parts as "Rotor, Nacelle, Electronics, Tower,
Foundation"; its only electrical item is 438.7 kg of control electronics, an
order of magnitude short of the 3–5 t a 2 MW turbine transformer weighs, and
it says outright that it excludes the grid connection. Its network connection
dataset is cable and trench.

**And ecoinvent cannot supply the asset.** Its four transformer activities are
two products with a market and a production each, and both are *electronics*:
"a typical high voltage use transformer in electronic modules has an average
weight of 280 g … used in the information and communication technology" — and
30 g for the low-voltage one. There is no substation, switchgear or power
transformer dataset at any rating. Scaling a 280 g component up to stand for a
57 t substation unit is a factor of 205,000 and runs about 2× high. So all
three transformers here — the two generation step-ups and the grid intake —
are assembled from a published bill of materials, the way the hydrogen tank
is, and nothing in the optimiser's default path scores ecoinvent's transformer
any more (only ``transformers.SOLAR_BASIS = "legacy"`` still does, to
reproduce pre-2026 runs).

Wind — Leng et al. 2026
-----------------------
    H. Leng, X. Zhou, J. Chen, D. Chen, M. Li, Y. Lin, Z. Yue, N. Zhong, "Life
    Cycle Assessment of an Onshore Wind Farm: Carbon Emission Evaluation and
    Mitigation Pathway Design", Processes 14(7), 1045 (2026), Supplementary
    Table S1. PowerChina Huadong Engineering.

Their Gaoyou farm is fifty 2 MW turbines, 100 MW, each with an S11-2200/35
box transformer; Table S1 gives the materials for all fifty as one bill.
Functional unit **1 MW of wind connected** = the bill ÷ 100, so it scales
exactly (one unit per turbine). Independently checked against Teffera et al.
(2021), Int J LCA 26:76–96, Table 5 — three Ethiopian farms, 228–333 kg
CO₂e/MW/year on this study's basis; Leng sits inside that band. Leng's units
are wound for 35 kV, above the medium-voltage band; a 20 kV unit of the same
rating is lighter, so their mass errs HIGH — the safe direction.

Solar — IEA PVPS Task 12, T12-33:2026
-------------------------------------
    M. Goetz, R. Deuber, N. Gazbour, P.H. Brailovsky, S. Nold, M.
    Marchand-Lasserre, R. Frischknecht, A.A. Khan, G. Bovo, M. Stucki (2026),
    "Life Cycle Inventories of Photovoltaic Systems", IEA PVPS Task 12, Report
    T12-33:2026, July 2026. DOI 10.69766/WJTE1771. Table 49 (the unit) and
    Table 50 (four of them per 10 MWp plant). Workbook shipped at
    optimisation/data/IEA-PVPS-T12-33-2026-LCI-PV-SupplyChains.xlsx.

The unit is wound **20 / 0.4 kV**, which is ``TX_SITE_COLLECTION_KV`` and the
inverter's LV terminals exactly, so no voltage adjustment is needed. The count
is *read off* Table 50 — "10 MW utility-scale electrical BoS including 4
units 2.5 MW transformers", 0.4 per MWp — which retires the DC/AC ratio and
power factor the old solar path assumed. The magnetic core is grain-oriented
electrical steel, which no LCI database carries; the report disaggregates it
into converter-route steel + MG-silicon + hot and cold rolling.

**A unit error in the source workbook, corrected.** The hardboard cell reads
36.96 with unit m³ ≈ 47 tonnes, eight times the whole transformer. Its own
comment reads "Al × 0.115 × 0.52 = 36.96 kg", and the end-of-life sheet's
paper row is 71.07 kg = 34.11 kraft + 36.96 pressboard, so the cell is kg
mislabelled as m³: 36.96 kg = 0.0291 m³ at hardboard's ~1,270 kg/m³. The bill
then sums to 5,670.0 kg against the report's "approximately 5,680";
``check()`` holds it within 0.5 %. (Until 21 Oct 2026 the row was back-solved
to 46.9 kg to hit 5,680 exactly, which reconciled on the wrong lever.)

Grid intake — Leng et al. 2026, the farm's main transformer
-----------------------------------------------------------
The same Table S1 also bills the Gaoyou farm's grid-end **main transformer,
XZ11-100000/110**: one 100 MVA unit stepping the 35 kV collection bus up to
110 kV, 71,458.6 kg = 714.6 kg/MVA. That is the only published bill of
materials in this study for a transformer of grid-intake class, so it is the
basis of ``cap_grid``'s embodied carbon: functional unit **1 MVA of
grid-intake transformer capacity** = the bill ÷ 100, mapped through the same
``TX_MATERIAL_PROCESSES`` as the wind units (the "Iron" reading is the same
judgement). ``optimisation/grid_connection.py`` scores it, applies N-1
redundancy and the power factor, and amortises it.

**The voltage judgement.** A 110 kV unit fits a GB **132 kV** EHV/DNO
connection, which is the common case for a ~100 MW data centre. For a site
connected at **275/400 kV** it errs LOW: supergrid transformers carry more
insulation and are heavier per MVA. Leng's unit is used for every site as the
default; it is stated in DATA_GAPS.md rather than varied by voltage.

**Materials only, because that is all Leng publish.** Their Table S1 is a
materials bill, S2 is transport and S3 is civils; no factory energy appears
for either transformer (checked against the SI and main text, 21 Oct 2026).
Their own 342 t CO₂e for this unit against ~275 t here is a scoring
difference — ecoinvent 3.11 with RoW steel proxies against 3.9.1 apos GLO
markets — not a dropped flow. The civils and installation Leng attribute to
the transformers (Table S3) are in: the box-transformer foundations (21 Oct)
and the electrical installation (section steel, terminal blocks, welding rod,
lead seals; 22 Oct) on the wind step-ups, per MW of the farm; the booster
station's **outdoor venue** — the 110 kV switchyard's site formation,
foundation beams, formwork, concrete, water and rebar, Leng's own 34.4 % of
the station — as its own activity per MW of connection (decision D2,
22 Oct 2026: the station serves 100 MW through one transformer, so its yard
scales with the connection, not the MVA). The station's three *buildings*
(control, auxiliary, production: 64.7 %) are treated as covered by Zhang's
facility building, which already houses the data centre's electrical rooms —
a stated substitution, not an omission. The station-wide construction
machinery (0.9 %) is listed once for all four projects, so its share is
pro-rated to the switchyard from Leng's own figure and carried on the
connection's coefficient (``exclusions.py``).

Battery and fuel cell — Jasper et al. 2026's mass on the IEA composition
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
A battery's PCS and a fuel cell's inverters put out LOW voltage too, so each
container needs the same LV → 20 kV step. Jasper et al. (2026)'s liquid-cooled
CSS bill (``bess.py``) lists one "transformer, for grid connection" of
**5,500 kg per 1,600 kW container**. That mass is spread over the IEA PVPS
20/0.4 kV unit's composition, forming and factory energy per kg.

**A stated substitution, on technological representativeness** (22 Oct 2026).
Jasper do give a per-kg recipe (air-cooled sheet rows 225–236; until 21 Oct
this module wrongly said they did not). Their §2.4.3 says it is derived from
Hunziker et al. (2020): a **630 kVA** line-frequency transformer with an
**on-load tap changer**, scaled by mass to the 1,800 kVA unit the container
needs. The IEA unit is a current **2,500 kVA, 20/0.4 kV oil-immersed
distribution transformer**, built from product documentation, at exactly the
step the container makes. The parent source's recipe is set aside because it
represents a different machine, not because it is missing. Jasper's recipe
scores 7.85 kg CO₂e/kg against 4.57 here (+72 %), most of the gap being its
0.09 kg/kg of control electronics, plausibly the tap changer's; it is carried
as the sensitivity case (SOURCES.md). Hunziker 2020 is not held, so the link
between the tap changer and the electronics row is inferred.

One activity, **per MW of inverter rating**, serves the
battery (``cap_batt_p``) and the fuel cell (``cap_fc``; one container of
``fuel_cell.FC_KW_PER_CONTAINER`` with the same 500 kW inverters), each
amortised over the asset's own life. Closed as negligible on 4 Sep 2026 and
modelled on 15 Oct: once the inventory and loss machinery existed, leaving
them out was a one-way bias against the generation chains, which pay for
theirs.

What is deliberately NOT here (all four): the grid-*export* transformer
charged to generation (this study's generation is behind the meter; Leng's
grid-end unit is used for the grid *intake* instead, charged per MW of
``cap_grid`` by ``grid_connection.py``); any step between the collection
network and the data centre (both sit in the medium-voltage band); switchgear
and protection (absent from the grid intake too, so a level shift rather than
a bias); losses; end-of-life. **Manufacturing energy** is in the solar bill
(~6 % of it) and in neither Leng bill, because Leng do not publish it;
materials-only wind and solar land within 1 %. **Civils**: the wind units
carry Leng's box-transformer foundations and the solar units the IEA PVPS
transformer station building, both since 21 Oct 2026.

What the optimiser reads: ``optimisation/transformers.py`` scores the two
step-ups and amortises them over ``dc_config.TX_ASSET_LIFE_YEARS``;
``optimisation/grid_connection.py`` scores the grid intake and amortises it
over its own ``ASSET_LIFE_YEARS``.

children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 23 Oct 2026.** Leng publish no factory energy; the cut-off register tests it at 0.14 % of wind's carbon (upper estimate), so it passes and stays out. Introduced by closing the solar half. **Corrected 21 Oct 2026:** Leng publish **no** factory energy for either transformer — Table S1 is materials, S2 transport, S3 civils — so there was never a published figure to take; their 342 t for the main unit against ~275 t here is ecoinvent 3.11 with RoW steel proxies against 3.9.1 apos, not a dropped flow. IEA PVPS T12-33:2026 give process energy explicitly (2,368 kWh + 9,904 MJ per 2.5 MVA unit) and it is taken, because excluding published data is the worse error. Process energy is ~6 % of the solar unit, so the two technologies agree within ~1 % materials-only and within 6 % as charged — but **wind now errs low relative to solar** by that margin. Closing it needs a wind-transformer inventory with manufacturing energy (none held); the IEA per-kg energy could stand in as an ASSUMED proxy.

children.name: Grid-intake transformer is a 110 kV unit
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed by the user 23 Oct 2026 as a stated judgement**: Leng's 110 kV unit fits a 132 kV connection and errs low for 275/400 kV sites. `grid_connection.py` charges `cap_grid` with Leng et al. (2026)'s grid-end main transformer, XZ11-100000/110 — **100 MVA wound for 110 kV**, 714.6 kg/MVA, materials only — for **every** site. That fits a GB **132 kV** EHV/DNO connection, the common case for a ~100 MW data centre. For a site connected to the transmission system at **275 or 400 kV** it errs **low**: supergrid transformers carry more insulation and are heavier per MVA (the uncited figure this replaced was 1.25 t/MVA for a 400 kV, 240 MVA SGT). It is not switched on `transmission_connected` because no bill of materials for a GB supergrid transformer has been found; a 275/400 kV EPD or BoM would close it. Like the wind units, the inventory is Chinese and excludes Leng's factory electricity (their own figure for this unit is 342 t CO₂e against ~275 t here), so it errs low on that count too. Small either way: the whole term is 137.7 kg CO₂e/MW/year, ~0.7 % of wind's per-MW burden.

children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: Source now identified and used. The FES *Economics Methodology report* states NESO's Li-ion capex is *"a combination of Modo survey data with CAPEX data from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory"*, citing **NREL, Cost Projections for Utility-Scale Battery Storage: 2023 Update (June 2023)**. Modo's own model assumptions are published openly at docs.modoenergy.com and are already in real 2025 GBP, so NREL was not needed: **£300/kW + £100/kWh**, WACC 5.0 % real, 15 y life, 10,000 cycles to 67 % capacity. children.name: Transmission connection embodied carbon
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **305.0 kg CO₂e/MW/year since 26 Oct 2026** (286.9 from 22 Oct): the transformer below (137.7), the switchyard's civils per MW of connection from Leng Table S3's outdoor venue (98.6; decision D2), its share of Leng's construction machinery (4.9, his own figure pro-rated), and estimates carried from the cut-off register because they fail 1 % against this denominator: switchgear and protection, and factory energy (45.8), and since 26 Oct Teffera Table 5's HV bay steelwork and grid-connection hardware (18.1). Before that, built in `grid_connection.py`: **137.7 kg CO₂e/MW/year** since 14 Oct, from a bill of materials: Leng et al. (2026) Table S1's grid-end main transformer **XZ11-100000/110** (100 MVA, 110 kV, 71,458.6 kg = 714.6 kg/MVA), built as `transformer foreground/grid_intake_transformer_per_mva` by `optimiser_lca/stepup_transformers.py` on the wind step-ups' material mapping — **2,753 kg CO₂e/MVA** materials-only (3.85 kg CO₂e/kg; copper is 23.5 % of the mass and half the carbon) — × 2 for N-1 ÷ power factor 1.0, over a 40-year life. Was **333.5**, from ecoinvent's `market for transformer, high voltage use` (5.34 kg CO₂e/kg, a 280 g electronics part) at an uncited 1.25 t/MVA DERIVED from a GB 400 kV supergrid transformer — so −59 %: the per-kg factor falls 28 % and the mass per MVA 43 %. About 0.7 % of wind's per-MW annual burden — small, but it is what makes `cap_grid` visible to the carbon objective and therefore no longer degenerate. A floor, not an estimate: switchgear, protection, civils, the bay, manufacturing energy, losses and end-of-life are not counted, and the 2 km line term is reported but not charged per MW. **Voltage judgement**: Leng's 110 kV unit fits a GB 132 kV EHV/DNO connection, the common case for a ~100 MW data centre, and is used for every site; for 275/400 kV transmission-connected sites it errs **low** — see the open row *Grid-intake transformer is a 110 kV unit*.

children.name: Step-up transformer inventory is an electronics part
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: ecoinvent's four transformer activities are two products, and both are electronics: its own comments say a high-voltage-use transformer "in electronic modules" averages **280 g** and a low-voltage one **30 g**, used "in the information and communication technology". There is no `substation`, no `switchgear` and no power transformer at any rating in ecoinvent 3.9.1 — searched, and recorded under *Checked and confirmed absent*. Wind previously scaled the 280 g part up by **205,000×**; it now reads a bill of materials built as a foreground activity in `2.tech_lca_foreground.ipynb` from Leng et al. (2026) Table S1. **Solar is now closed too**, from a source that postdates the wind fix: IEA PVPS Task 12 **T12-33:2026** (July 2026) Table 49 gives an oil-immersed **2.5 MVA** unit at **5,680 kg**, wound **20/0.4 kV** — which is `TX_SITE_COLLECTION_KV` and the inverter's LV terminals exactly, so unlike the wind units (wound for 35 kV, mass taken as erring high) no voltage adjustment is applied. Built as `transformer foreground/solar_inverter_stepup_per_mwp`. The invented unit survives only as `transformers.SOLAR_BASIS = "legacy"`. **The grid intake is closed as well** (14 Oct): `grid_connection.py` now reads Leng's 100 MVA main transformer as `transformer foreground/grid_intake_transformer_per_mva` (row above), so nothing on the default path scores ecoinvent's transformer any more.

children.name: Specific mass below ~10 MVA
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: The old basis transcribed 1,434.5 kg/MVA from a 40 MVA unit and could not transfer it down, so turbine-level step-ups were **not counted at all** — and they are the larger half. Leng et al. (2026) Table S1 gives the bill for fifty 2.2 MVA units directly, so no transfer is needed, and the curve it completes is now measured: **2,566 kg/MVA at 2.2 MVA, 1,434 at 40, 715 at 100**. Teffera et al. (2021) Table 5 corroborates the level. **Solar is now closed on the same curve**: IEA PVPS T12-33:2026 gives **2,272 kg/MVA at 2.5 MVA**, and Badza et al. (2023)'s Zagtouli plant an independent **2,219 kg/MVA at 2.33 MVA** — three inventories within 15 % at the inverter-station rating. The count is **read off** Table 50 (4 units per 10 MWp) rather than derived, retiring the ASSUMED `SOLAR_DC_AC_RATIO` and `POWER_FACTOR`. Coefficients now land at solar **296.0** vs wind **278.7** kg CO₂e/unit/year.

children.name: The solar generation coefficient is built on rooftop hardware
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: `renewables.SOLAR_EMBODIED_BASES` defaulted to `iea_pvps_2023_mono_si`, whose reference system is a **3 kWp rooftop array** — so `cap_solar`, a utility-scale MWp, was priced with roof rails, a domestic string inverter, no perimeter fence, no plant-scale site cabling and no land. It was also the one coefficient not on ecoinvent 3.9.1 apos (IEA PVPS use UVEK in SimaPro, under **recycled-content** allocation — a different system model, which SOURCES.md had not recorded). Default is now **`smith_2024_upv_fixed_tilt`**: Smith et al. (2024) NREL/TP-7A40-87372 Appendix A, the whole c-Si chain plus BOS, **rescored on ecoinvent 3.9.1 apos** as a foreground so it is APOS by construction rather than transcribed off another background. **895.3 t CO₂e/MWp, 22.0 g CO₂e/kWh, 23,561 kg CO₂e/MWp/year** against 1,048.2 / 25.8 / 27,585 — a 14.6 % cut, driven by the balance of system rather than the module: the module actually rises (591 → 684 t/MWp) while the BOS more than halves, because a 3 kWp roof amortises its inverter, cabling and mounting over 3 kW rather than megawatts. The BAFU-vs-ecoinvent objection that made this look hard applied to the *2026 IEA report*, not to Smith, whose provider strings are ecoinvent-native and resolve 93 % directly. Fixed tilt via IEA PVPS T12-33:2026 `Z-PV-239` (20°), which is **heavier** than Smith's tracker, not lighter. Verified: 290/290 values transcribed, 251 rows association-checked (249 clean), all four non-zero-GWP biosphere flows included, and the module reproduces Smith's own stated EPEAT result of >630 kg CO₂e/kWdc. Residual: construction transport excluded by scope, which **understates by ~1.5 %**. See `data/UPV-DEFERRED-ISSUES.md`.

children.name: Bought green H₂ carried grid-electrolysis carbon
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: Scoring `pem_op_hermesmann_1kg_h2` whole charged bought green **17.001 kg CO₂e/kg** — dirtier than grey SMR, and dirtier than the LP plugging its own electrolyser into the grid — because the activity links 54 kWh/kg to ecoinvent's GB *grid* market at 311.22 g CO₂e/kWh. Green hydrogen is defined by renewable input, so the coefficient is now assembled as `foreground_fixed + kwh_per_kg × I` with `I` named in `h2_prices.GREEN_H2_ELECTRICITY_BASES`. Default `ecoinvent_onshore` — this study's own unrestated GB onshore wind activity, 14.466 g/kWh → **0.976 kg CO₂e/kg**. Every basis is renewable and the grid is deliberately not among them, so behind-the-meter pricing can no longer be paired with grid carbon; the old value survives as `LEGACY_GREEN_H2_GWP_KGCO2E_PER_KG` for reproducing prior runs. The grid-connected variant is renewable too, and differs by **delivery**: the grid's own high-voltage delivery terms, a 3.38 % loss gross-up plus 1.93 g CO₂e/kWh of network carbon (`optimiser_lca.grid.DELIVERY`, re-checked by `check_grid_delivery()`), giving **1.107 kg CO₂e/kg** against 0.976 behind the meter (1.469 on the low-voltage basis used until 13 Oct). Not a new judgement: 76 % of that 311 g/kWh is one gas dataset `optimiser_lca/grid.py` does not use for this study's own grid (gas is scored on the combined-cycle plant), and grid electrolysis is already modelled properly as `grid_h2`. At 17.001 the row was strictly Pareto-dominated on both axes, so every bought-green run to date was dead code. Residual caveats in `SOURCES.md`: the seller's plant is a proxy build on this study's own PEM inventory, and the price's CF 0.50 does not match the capital amortisation's 0.732. Delivery *compression* is no longer excluded — see the row below, where the ~0.761 kg/kg estimated here turned out to be wrong by 33x because it assumed a grid-powered compressor

children.name: PV embodied carbon is 2008-vintage
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: ecoinvent 3.9.1's GB open-ground PV activity is Solarpark El Tesoro, **installed 2008**, at a 12.95 % module — it restated to 56.7 g CO₂e/kWh, ~10× onshore wind. Not fixable by upgrading: the plant inventory is **byte-identical in ecoinvent 3.10.1**, and GB has no other utility-scale PV activity in either version. Default basis is now **IEA PVPS Task 12 2023 update, mono-Si — 1,048 t CO₂e/MWp, 25.8 g CO₂e/kWh** at this study's yield and lifetime, 4.6× wind rather than 10.1×. `renewables.SOLAR_EMBODIED_BASES` keeps `ecoinvent` selectable to reproduce older runs, and `build_tech(solar_basis=...)` threads the choice to the LP. IEA PVPS's multi-Si figure is recorded in `SOURCES.md` as evidence that the gap is manufacturing vintage rather than module efficiency, but is not offered as a basis — at ~1 % of the 2023 market it fails the same test ecoinvent does. **Closed only against the 2008 vintage, not against the mount type**: IEA PVPS's reference is a 3 kWp **rooftop** array, and it is the one coefficient in the study not scored on ecoinvent 3.9.1 apos. Both are now tracked as their own open row above (*"The solar generation coefficient is still built on rooftop hardware"*) rather than as residual caveats here, because the hardware gap is material rather than cosmetic — a utility plant carries steel tables, a fence, plant-scale cabling and land that a 3 kWp roof does not.

children.name: Bought hydrogen carried no delivery compression
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: `dc_model`'s tank balance took `h2_buy` at coefficient 1.0 while self-produced hydrogen paid `h2_storage.compression_kwh_per_kg` to enter the same vessel — an asymmetry that was one-directional and favoured buying. Every bought colour now carries compression to **200 bar** tube-trailer pressure at the seller's gate, in **both** objectives, so this does not join the study's standing list of things charged in carbon and free in cost. Reuses `h2_storage.compression_kwh_per_kg`, so the buyer's compression and the seller's are one thermodynamics rather than two. The intensity is colour-specific and that is the point: green's compressor runs on the same renewable basis and `grid_share` as its own electrolyser, because a plant defined by sitting behind a renewable meter cannot compress on grid power; every other colour is a fossil plant already scored against the GB grid its activity links to. **The result inverts the expectation recorded above.** This register carried ~0.761 kg CO₂e/kg as the term's likely size for green, which would have been 78 % of production and might have re-dominated the row — but that figure assumed grid electricity. Charged coherently green's compression is **0.023 kg/kg (+1.9 %)**, and the colour it actually moves is **blue at 0.451 kg/kg (+14.5 %)**, with grey +4.3 % and turquoise +8.3 %. See `SOURCES.md`

children.name: Battery LCA as a sized asset
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Rebuilt 14 Oct** as a grid battery, not an EV pack: `optimiser_lca/bess.py` builds Jasper et al. 2026's liquid-cooled LFP container (cells, modules, racks, container, liquid cooling, fire suppression) around Voß et al. 2025's LFP cell, made in China, on ecoinvent 3.9.1. **101.11 kg CO₂e per kWh nameplate** (21 Oct 2026, with Jasper's concrete block and Voß's in-China material legs; 97.75 at the rebuild), ÷ an **assumed** 0.90 usable fraction = **112.3 per usable kWh**, + **31.9 kg CO₂e/kW** (PCS, unchanged). Was 98.2 on ecoinvent's EV traction pack with no enclosure and no usable-fraction correction. Open: the cell is the soft spot (Jasper's 3.11 cell is 20 % higher on the same bill); the factory energy is Degen's via Jasper, not Voß's own; 5 MWh containers would take ~3 kg/kWh off. See `SOURCES.md`.

children.name: On-site switchgear, and its insulating gas
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Superseded 22 Oct 2026** by the cut-off register (see *Switchgear carbon*, closed 23 Oct). **Closed 4 Sep as negligible** with the other balance-of-plant items — the SF₆ asymmetry below is inside the same bound. Neither `transformers.py` nor `grid_connection.py` counts switchgear, so it is a level shift rather than a bias between building and importing. But it is not symmetric in one respect: ecoinvent's `market for electricity, medium voltage` states that SF₆ from **high voltage level switchgear is allocated to the electricity demand on medium voltage**, so imported power pays for switchgear gas and on-site generation pays nothing. Small — Teffera puts MV + HV switchgear at 0.61 t/MW against a plant transformer's 1.08 t/MW, and a site's own bays are a tiny share of the national fleet the 0.025 g CO₂e/kWh network term covers. Points the same way as the losses row below, and stacks with it. Closing it needs a switchgear EPD **and** a bay count, which is a network-design outcome like `sites.connection_limit_mw`.

children.name: Fuel cell duty cost
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: Found by `audit.py`. Carbon charged stack and BoP on `max(calendar, duty)` while cost charged a BoP calendar annuity only, so above 2,400 h/yr BoP wear was free in cost and the fuel cell line up to 39 % low. **Closed 12 Oct**: `h2_capex.fuel_cell_costs()` now splits BoP like the stack — `A·(CRF + o − 1/L)` on capacity plus `A` per `fc_bop_units` — which is exactly the old annuity when calendar binds and within 2 % of the exact CRF when duty does (`test_fuel_cell_bop_cost_increment_tracks_the_exact_annuity`). `audit.py` now checks each replacement variable on its own, since pooling them is how the half-fix passed. Still open, as plan §1 step 2: the stack is charged undiscounted per replacement, and fixed opex sits on the BoP share only.

children.name: Grid gas scored on the conventional plant
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 13 Oct.** A search query plus a hit index (`GRID_CANDIDATE_INDEX["GAS"] = 3`) landed on ecoinvent's GB conventional plant (558 g/kWh) though the query asked for combined cycle (387). Sources are now exact identities in `optimiser_lca.grid.SOURCES`, every grid CSV records an id of its scoring basis, and `profiles` ignores series scored on another. All 20 series were re-scored from their recorded mix: London 2025 236.9 → 188.2 g/kWh (−21 %), grid-only baseline 16,131 → 13,010 t/yr.

children.name: Grid imports carried no network carbon, and two delivery bases
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 13 Oct.** The grid series was generation × a flat 3.16 % loss with no network carbon, while bought green H₂ paid *low-voltage* delivery (×1.0635 + 8.2125 g/kWh). Both now read one table, `optimiser_lca.grid.DELIVERY`, derived from ecoinvent's GB voltage chain by `derive_delivery()` and re-checked by `check_delivery()`: high voltage ×1.0338 + 1.93 g/kWh, medium ×1.0454 + 4.89, low ×1.1132 + 11.30. A site's voltage follows its connection (`network_charges.delivery_voltage`: transmission and every EHV band are high); the seller's is `h2_prices.GREEN_H2_SELLER_VOLTAGE` = high, **assumed**. The old low-voltage figures were short even for low voltage — the gross-up left CHP and import kWh out of "generation", the network left out the HV market's N₂O (corona discharge, 1.41 of the 1.93 g) and the direct SF₆. Effect: about +2 g/kWh on every region's grid; bought green at 100 % grid share 1.469 → 1.107 kg CO₂e/kg. The TODO's "half again on a Scottish grid" assumed the 8.2 g low-voltage network; at high voltage it is +3.4 % on North Scotland
`optimiser_lca/grid.py` §5

children.name: Grid import split was ecoinvent's, on every region
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 13 Oct.** Imports were split FR 63 / NL 30 / IE 7 % — the shares inside ecoinvent's GB market, pre-North Sea Link and pre-Viking Link — whatever the region and whatever was flowing. GB's 2025 interconnector imports were FR 51, NO 21, DK 11, BE 9, NL 7, IE 1 %, and NESO's regional import share is geographic. Now each half-hour's imports are split by Elexon FUELHH interconnector flows, weighted per region by a non-negative least-squares fit of the region's API import share on the ten links' flows over 2025 (`grid_build.fit_import_attribution`, R² 0.18–0.71; North Scotland, South Scotland and South Wales, importing 0.6–2.9 %, take the national flows). London's imports are FR 74 / BE 16 / NL 8 / NO 2 % (R² 0.70); East England's are NL 60 / FR 29 / BE 10 %; the North East's NO 88 %. London 2025 −29 g/kWh, East England +10, and the North East's June week 82 → 31. NO and DK are scored on their own HV markets (22 and 207 g/kWh), as ecoinvent's "import from XX" activities are those markets under another name
`optimiser_lca/grid.py` §2b

children.name: Grid solar share and pumped storage on unsuitable datasets
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 13 Oct.** The grid's solar was ecoinvent's 2008 El Tesoro plant (79.8 g/kWh), the one rejected for `cap_solar`; it is now the Smith 2024 plant at ecoinvent's GB yield (961 kWh/kWp/yr, 30 y), **30.9 g/kWh** (`upv_gb_grid_fleet_1kwh`). Utility fixed tilt stands in for a fleet about half rooftop. Pumped storage (466 g/kWh, its 1.43 kWh of pumping taken from ecoinvent's 2018 GB market on the conventional gas plant) is now its own plant and reservoir (50.5 g/kWh) plus 1.43 kWh of the half-hour's other generation. The API reports storage as 0 % in every regional series built so far, so only solar moved: −2.9 g/kWh on London
`optimiser_lca/grid.py` §1, §3

children.name: Balance of plant judged negligible
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 4 Sep, revised 15 Oct.** Originally: battery and fuel-cell step-up transformers; connection and step-up switchgear; the data centre's own electrical distribution — sized against the North Norfolk 100 MW run, all together at most ~1.6 % of total carbon at the knee point and under 0.2 % at minimum cost, so none could move a ranking. **The two step-ups are now counted** (15 Oct): once the transformer inventory and the loss model existed, leaving them out was a one-way bias against the generation chains, which pay for theirs. `transformer foreground/containerised_lv_stepup_per_mw` — Jasper et al. 2026's "transformer, for grid connection", **5,500 kg per 1,600 kW container** (3,437.5 kg/MW, on the measured curve), spread over the IEA PVPS 20/0.4 kV unit's composition and process energy as a stated substitution (Jasper's own per-kg recipe is Hunziker 2020's 630 kVA unit, SOURCES.md): **15,674 kg CO₂e per MW** of inverter rating, 4.56 kg CO₂e/kg, identical per kg to solar's unit by construction. Charged per MW of `cap_batt_p` over the battery's 15-y life (**1,045 kg CO₂e/MW/yr**: +49 % on the power term, ~+3 % on a 4-hour battery) and per MW of `cap_fc` over the BoP calendar life (**784 kg/MW/yr** at 20 y, +6.6 % on the fuel cell's per-MW capital; a swept BoP life carries its transformer with it). Amortising over the asset's own life rather than the transformer's 35 y errs high, the study's convention. Losses at Reg. 548/2014 Tier 2 (1,600 kVA interpolated; 1,000 kVA): no-load **0.066 % / 0.069 %** of rating every hour — the fuel cell's unit **kept energised on standby** (decision, 15 Oct), ~2–3 % of a backup unit's own output — and load loss 0.75 % / 0.76 % of throughput at full loading, linearised at ASSUMED loadings x_eff **0.5** (battery, both ways) and **1.0** (fuel cell); all three swept in `sensitivity.CARBON_KNOBS`. **Since 22 Oct 2026 every one of these is on the cut-off register** (`optimiser_lca/exclusions.py`, ASSUMPTIONS §8): container switchgear (battery, fuel cell) and the grid connection's switchgear fail the 1 % test against their own technology and are carried as estimates on the coefficient; the wind and solar step-ups' switchgear and the facility's MV/LV distribution pass and stay out, stated. The battery enclosure was closed with them and has since been counted anyway (the 14 Oct grid-battery inventory carries it). Hydrogen compressor *carbon* was closed the same day (~12.8 t CO₂e per 300 kW unit, 0.01 % of the tank); its cost is still open.

children.name: Conversion losses are not modelled anywhere
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 14 Oct.** The node balance treated a kWh at a generator's terminals as a kWh at the data centre, while imports already paid their delivery losses — on-site generation flattered, one way. `optimisation/conversion_losses.py` now charges the losses of the three transformers the study already inventories, at the GB legal maxima: retained Regulation (EU) No 548/2014 Annex I, Tier 2, Table I.1 (2,000 kVA: Pk 15,000 W, Po 1,305 W; 2,500 kVA: 18,500 W, 1,575 W) and Table I.7 (≥ 100 MVA: PEI 99.770 %), read on legislation.gov.uk. Wind's 2.2 MVA step-up (interpolated; wound for 35 kV, above the table's class): no-load 0.071 % of capacity, load loss 0.68 % of output at full loading; solar's 2.5 MVA unit: 0.063 % and 0.74 %; grid intake: 0.092 % of the connection and 0.072 % of imports. No-load is a node demand on installed capacity; load loss is linearised at the profile's energy-weighted loading Σcf²/Σcf (exact in energy when the unit carries its availability profile, slightly high under curtailment). **Assumed**: the 100 MVA unit's peak-efficiency loading k_PEI = 0.4 (which splits PEI into Po and Pk) and the intake's loading x_eff = 0.5. The lost energy carries no coefficient of its own — it is generated or imported by plant the LP already charges. Inverter/PCS losses stay inside the battery's RTE and the fuel cell's net efficiency
`conversion_losses.py`, `dc_model.loss_factors`

children.name: Unserved load carried no carbon
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 14 Oct.** Cost charged unserved MWh at VoLL; carbon charged nothing, so a min-GWP solve with any unserved allowance shed the dirtiest hours as an emissions cut (455.7 against a 236.9 kg/MWh mean on the old grid), and every g/kWh and £/MWh divided by gross demand. Unserved MWh are now charged in carbon the same way as in cost, as a penalty — VoLL at the study's carbon price, £100,000/MWh ÷ £78.96/t = **1,266 t CO₂e/MWh** (`dc_model.VOLL_KGCO2E_PER_MWH`). Intensities are reported on **served** demand with both penalties off (`dc_model.intensities`); totals still carry them, as cost always has. `audit.py` now checks unserved and bought H₂ as streams, which is how this was confirmed
`dc_model.py`

children.name: Wind life extension and net yield
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 14 Oct**, two halves. (1) *Parts.* ecoinvent's turbine is a 20-y machine with no replacements, amortised here over DESNZ's 35 y (25–40 by case). Wind capital is now grossed up for what it takes to get there (`renewables.WIND_LIFE_EXTENSION`): servicing at **4 % per 20 operating years**, pro rata (Vestas V136/V162 LCAs Fig 7, "replacements/servicing" ~4 %; Siemens Gamesa SG 6.2-170 EPD O&M ~5 %), plus **one overhaul** once the life passes a 25-y design life — gearbox, main shaft and a blade set, **20.5 %** of production GWP (V136 9 + 9 %, V162 8 + 15 %). The overhaul is the study's own construction; no LCA itemises a 20→35-y extension. Central onshore restates **5.77 → 7.32 g CO₂e/kWh** (`gwp_wind` 19,244 → 24,416 kg/MW/yr), above IPCC AR5's ~7 g floor. `build_tech(wind_life_extension=…)` takes `none` / `servicing` / `servicing_overhaul`. (2) *Yield.* ninja's single-turbine series is scaled by `profiles.WIND_NET_FACTOR` **0.851** = availability 0.969 (Arup 2024 §5.8.2) × wake 0.91 (§5.8.4) × electrical 0.98 (Vestas 2.5 %, less the step-up now in `conversion_losses.py`) × performance 0.985 (assumed). **Residual caveat**: Staffell & Pfenninger's bias correction is fitted to metered fleet output, so if a point series carries it, part of this is counted twice — the API's metadata does not say. Coastal sites stay above Arup's 41.3 % high case even at 0.851, so it does not over-correct there. `build_series(wind_net_factor=1.0)` reproduces old runs
`renewables.py`, `profiles.py`

children.name: Fossil hydrogen on ecoinvent's 2018 GB grid
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 14 Oct.** SMR, SMR-CCS, the CCS train and methane pyrolysis linked their electricity to ecoinvent's `market for electricity, high voltage` [GB] (gas on the conventional plant), and bought fossil H₂'s trailer compression was charged at the 311 g/kWh low-voltage market — the last grid figures in the study not on `optimiser_lca.grid`. A new foreground, `grid foreground/gb_grid_2025_hv_delivered` (`optimiser_lca/gb_grid.py`), is one kWh of the study's own grid: NESO's GB-wide 2025 mix (API region 18, time-mean), each fuel on `grid.SOURCES`, imports on the national interconnector split, delivered at high voltage — **141.87 g CO₂e/kWh**, exactly the series mean. All four fossil activities and the fossil compressor now take it. Turquoise, 10.29 kWh/kg, falls most: production 5.46 → 3.92 kg/kg
`optimiser_lca/gb_grid.py`

children.name: Gas-route carbon balance
children.section: Closed since the register was opened
cells: **Closed 14 Oct** (the audit's "unverified" blue item, checked against the inventory rather than the paper). Every carbon atom in the gas leaves as CO₂. ecoinvent's GB high-pressure gas carries 0.741 kg fossil C/kg at 0.735 kg/m³ — **1.996 kg CO₂ per m³** — and Hermesmann's exports do not close on it: SMR 4.85 m³ → 9.686 kg, emits 9.0 (**0.679 short**); SMR-CCS 5.33 m³ → 10.636 kg, captures 8.01 and emits 0.99 — the same 9.0 as grey on 10 % more gas (**1.637 short**). The shortfall is charged as fossil CO₂ to air: the capture-solvent steam is raised in a flue the inventory's capture does not reach. The CCS step's 0.0154 kg diesel per kg CO₂ was linked as a product and never burned; it is now `diesel, burned in building machine` at 42.8 MJ/kg. Production: grey 10.46 → **11.31**, blue 3.12 → **5.15** kg CO₂e/kg (+65 %; the audit's 11–48 % bracket used the SMR route's own ratio, which hid grey's own shortfall). Delivered with compression: grey 11.51, blue 5.36, turquoise 4.13, green 1.06. `test_gas_routes_close_their_carbon_balance`
`optimiser_lca/hydrogen.py`

children.name: H2 tank leakage
children.section: Open — public source identified, not yet pulled
cells: A compressed-gas storage standard, or a fugitive-emissions study (candidate, not yet read: Frazer-Nash Consultancy for BEIS, 2022, *Fugitive hydrogen emissions in a future hydrogen economy*); plus DESNZ/Warwick et al. 2022 for H₂'s own GWP100 (~11) if leakage is charged

`h2_storage.LEAKAGE_FRAC_PER_HOUR`, zero and **assumed**; overridable as `build_tech(tank_leakage_per_hour=…)`. **Bounded by sweep, 14 Oct**, over 0 / 0.01 / 0.1 %/day — itself an ASSUMED range, since nothing here states an order (reasoning in `SOURCES.md`, tank *Standing loss*). Same reference case and grid as *Battery standing loss* below (`optimisation_outputs/storage_loss_sweep.csv`). Tank leakage alone moves cost by at most +0.08 % and carbon by −0.04 to +0.03 %, the tank by −1.1 % (190.7 → 188.7 t at min cost; 167.3 t unchanged at min carbon). **It does not decide hydrogen-versus-battery at these magnitudes**, which this row used to assert: the min-carbon tank averages only ~8 % full, so a loss on the stock held has little to bite on. What the sweep does surface is the term the LP leaves out — leaked H₂ as a greenhouse gas. At 0.1 %/day that is ~26 t H₂/yr at min cost, **~290 t CO₂e/yr (0.46 %)** at GWP100 11, and ~5 t H₂, ~54 t CO₂e (0.10 %) at min carbon — larger than the energy-loss effect, and still in neither objective (reported in the CSV as `h2_leak_gwp100_t_per_year_NOT_IN_LP`). **Charged since 14 Oct**: `dc_model` now adds leaked H₂ to the carbon objective at GWP100 **11.6** (Sand et al. 2023; IPCC 2021 as implemented in ecoinvent has no factor for hydrogen, so this is a stated extension of the method), on `tank_leakage_per_hour × dt × stock`. Still zero by default, because leakage is
